answer: Dual-ledger anchoring stops Sybils in four steps. First, a newcomer anchors its key in two independent public ledgers, a code history and an on-chain record. Second, peers cross-check both records, matching timestamps and authorship, like pigment checked against a mirror image. Third, a mismatch burns a $35 deposit and freezes the key ninety days. Fourth, job limits rise only after sixty days of matched records. Faking 1,000 agents needs 2,000 forged histories plus $35,000 in deposits, all lost when caught. Trust grows like a willow: slow, visible, rooted in two soils at once.
